cases.understood: Ray from A to B with one reflection on a horizontal plane mirror; A height 5 cm, B height 20 cm, horizontal separation 20 cm.
cases.derivation: Reflect B across the mirror. The intersection of line A to virtual B with the mirror is 4 cm from the point directly below A, towards B: x=20*5/(5+20)=4 cm.
cases.limitations: A native finite-mirror ray illustration is possible with stated A and B locations; mirror length, chosen source emission, and point-target observation are not supplied as simulator components, and sampled ray hits do not automatically return precise mirror strike x.

cases.understood: A particle projectile with velocity v at angle alpha, image in a stationary inclined mirror at 60°, ask for the instant of zero relative image velocity.
cases.limitations: Requires trajectory, gravity, time-dependent position/velocity and relative reference-frame observation. Static 2D PhyDemo scene does not solve dynamics.

cases.understood: Incident ray initially parallel to plane mirror 2, reflecting first from mirror 1 then mirror 2, leaves parallel to mirror 1; determine mutual angle and total deviation.
cases.derivation: Let mirror 2 tangent angle 0° and mirror 1 tangent θ. Reflection directions: 0° -> 2θ -> -2θ. Outgoing parallel to mirror 1 requires -2θ ≡ θ (mod 180°), yielding θ=60° in the nondegenerate acute case and total direction change |2θ|=120°.
cases.limitations: Native ray reflections are supported but the problem specifies an inverse direction condition, not numerical mirror lengths or incident ray starting point; finite mirrors that share a vertex may violate the current segment-contact validator. Do not claim an exact native scene.

cases.understood: Two parallel plane mirrors separated 40 cm with object 10 cm from one; find object-to-image distances of the five closest virtual images.
cases.derivation: For reflecting planes x=0 and 40 cm and object x=10 cm, image positions generated by repeated reflections are x = 80k ± 10 cm, except the original x=+10. Sorted distinct virtual-image distances from the object begin 20, 60, 80, 80, and 100 cm.
cases.limitations: Two nonintersecting finite mirrors and a point source can show multiple native reflections, but source is an object idealization, lengths are not stated, and general tracing does not enumerate or certify multiple virtual-image positions.

cases.understood: Find minimum looking-glass size allowing an observer to see their whole 24 by 16 cm face, with one eye versus two eyes 8 cm apart.
cases.limitations: Needs extended 2D/3D face, eye/observer aperture, ray visibility and minimum mirror-size objective. Current point-source / passive crossing model does not measure this.

cases.understood: A moving object and moving vertical plane mirror have specified velocities; derive image velocity.
cases.limitations: Needs time-dependent kinematics / moving objects beyond static scene parameters. Native plane reflection alone does not provide image velocity.

cases.understood: A concave spherical mirror with f=25 cm and object 50 cm away is cut and halves separated transverse to the axis; determine displaced image arrangement.
cases.limitations: Requires curved spherical reflecting surfaces and decentring of mirror halves. A pair of plane mirrors or lenses would silently change the physics.

cases.understood: Parallel rays from air pass through water (n=4/3) and reflect from a concave mirror at 30 cm depth (R=40 cm); determine final image.
cases.limitations: Requires a refractive index boundary, spherical mirror and true collimated incident beam. None is exposed in the strict current authoring contract.

measurement: Prospective model interpretations, NOT independently graded. Mathematical conclusions not yet independently verified.
